nodes.short: reduction pass before a pull request
nodes.detail: Reviews a finished change for needless complexity and removes it. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs.

nodes.short: runs the checks, reports a verdict
nodes.detail: Has its own context window, so four hundred lines of build output never enter the session doing the implementation.

nodes.short: logs what the agent touched, and when
nodes.detail: Git records commits and GitHub records approvals; this covers the part nobody otherwise sees. Local only — committing it left the working tree permanently dirty and made git checkout refuse to switch branches.

nodes.short: formats the file just written
nodes.detail: Formatting is not worth a review comment or a turn of the agent's attention. A hook settles it silently and identically every time.

nodes.short: refuses dangerous shell commands
nodes.detail: Denies force-push, reset --hard, curl piped to a shell, and writes straight to the default branch. It matches the raw command string, which is why it also refuses prose that quotes those commands.

nodes.short: freezes an accepted intent or spec
nodes.detail: Once Status says accepted, the artifact stops being editable by an agent. Amending one is a proposal a human installs.

nodes.short: the agent cannot edit its own guardrails
nodes.detail: Denies writes to .github/workflows, .claude/settings.json and .claude/hooks. CI workflows define what runs without a human; an agent that can edit them can grant itself new powers.

nodes.short: wires the hooks — the agent cannot edit this
nodes.detail: Five hooks on two events. It carries no permissions block yet, which is intent 0050: the boundary between what the agent may and may not do is currently a sentence in a skill rather than a list in a file.

nodes.short: design and prose constraints for this site
nodes.detail: Institutional knowledge applied as a constraint rather than a prompt someone retypes — including the asset-path rule, which exists because that exact bug shipped once.

nodes.short: Stage 1 — the intent template and its rules
nodes.detail: States a problem, never a solution. Also holds the id rule: the number is the GitHub issue number, because incrementing from the directory listing produced two 0003s in a day.

nodes.short: the orchestrator — does the stage that is next
nodes.detail: Given an id it reads which artifacts exist and performs the one stage that follows, rather than being told which. --auto runs the remaining stages in one pull request; it may compress agreement, never manufacture it.

nodes.short: Stage 3 — turning a plan into a pull request
nodes.detail: What must pass, what the body has to say, and which commands a human needs next.

nodes.short: Stage 2 — the design template
nodes.detail: Its most valuable output is not the design but the numbered decisions, because those are what later work cites when it needs to diverge.

nodes.short: issue labelled → drafts an intent
nodes.detail: Triggers on labelled, never on opened. Applying a label needs write access, which makes the trigger a maintainer triaging rather than a stranger typing into a box.

nodes.short: cron; a breach opens an issue
nodes.detail: Stage 6, and the step that hands the loop back to a human. It opens the issue and deliberately does not label it: a breach is evidence, not a decision.

nodes.short: format, evals, diagram drift — builds nothing
nodes.detail: The process half of the pipeline, about four seconds. Runs on everything, because a change to docs or .claude can break a hook or an artifact without touching the site.

nodes.short: reviews a pull request, when asked
nodes.detail: workflow_dispatch only. It used to run on every pull request: 58 runs produced 2 comments, and none at all on the last fifteen. Kept because the one run that won its race found seven real things, so it is now something you ask for rather than something that fires and says nothing.

nodes.short: @claude mentions — the steering wheel
nodes.detail: The one place a stranger's words reach an agent. The action checks the triggering user has write access; that check is a default of the action, not a line in this file.

nodes.short: gated release to rashid.fr/sdlc/
nodes.detail: The build job has no credentials. The deploy job has them and cannot start until a named human approves. That asymmetry is the whole governance argument.

nodes.short: Monday: what is in flight, to Slack
nodes.detail: Runs npm run intents, which is a script and not a model — same answer every time, no tokens. Weekly rather than daily, because a digest that arrives every morning becomes wallpaper.

nodes.short: every pull request gets a live URL
nodes.detail: Uses a different FTP account from deploy: its user is chrooted to the preview directory and cannot reach the live site. Environments are about blast radius; approval is a separate axis.

nodes.short: npm audit — the agentic half is a stub
nodes.detail: A labelled shell, and the site says so. The agent step is written and commented out; a static site has almost no attack surface, and inventing a finding would be the dishonesty this repository argues against.

nodes.short: builds the site, crawls every link
nodes.detail: Stage 4, and the only thing allowed to say it works. Path-filtered to changes that could alter the built output, so editing a spec does not deploy a website.

nodes.short: pins Node 22.19.0
nodes.detail: Astro refuses Node 20. On the Windows laptop nvm use needs elevation and fails silently, so the PATH is prefixed instead of trusting the switch.

nodes.short: what healthy means, in numbers
nodes.detail: Availability, page weight and build time. The mechanism is real and the metrics are toy — there are no users, so there is no error rate to watch.

nodes.short: the problem, and what would be true once fixed
files, order of work, and how completion is proven
numbered design decisions and their reasons
structural assertions, zero tokens
nodes.detail: Asserts the guardrails still deny what they claim to deny and that generated artifacts keep their shape. No judgement of quality — that is the token-hungry half, and it is labelled as missing.

nodes.short: the commands, including the one that matters
nodes.detail: npm run verify builds, serves at the real base path, crawls every link and runs the evals. A Node script rather than shell glue, because anything with shell in it is a portability bug waiting for a reader on another OS.
